valueTypes.representation: Runtime null tag; not a declarable persistent SQL column type.
Shared signed 64-bit physical carrier. Logical INTEGER is signed 32-bit, BIGINT is signed 64-bit, and BOOLEAN is canonical 0/1.
Exact base-10 decimal with an Int64 coefficient and scale up to 18 digits of precision.

rules.notes: A migration target is one local CSharpDB database.
CSharpDB has no source-style namespace catalog; names must be flattened deterministically.
Typed SQL tables are supported.
Collections use the collection API and serialized document storage rather than SQL DDL.
Persistent columns retain a logical SQL type descriptor over INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB, or DECIMAL storage.
Primary and unique keys are supported subject to key type and collation rules.
Single and composite immediate foreign keys are supported with bounded actions.
Deterministic row-local check expressions are supported.
Ordinary column indexes are supported subject to type restrictions.
There is no standalone sequence catalog object.
A view body must parse, bind, and pass scratch execution before it is executable evidence.
Trigger timing, event, and body must be checked; WHEN is rejected with SyntaxError before catalog persistence.
Source database routines do not have a general automatic CSharpDB lowering contract.
Provider-specific objects require an explicit capability rule.
Identifiers are quoted when rendered, limited to 128 UTF-16 code units, and compared case-insensitively by catalogs.
Logical SQL declarations map to these persistent storage types; declared facets are retained and enforced.
Nullable and NOT NULL columns are supported.
Defaults must be NULL or compatible typed literals; arbitrary source expressions require analysis.
IDENTITY is limited to logical INTEGER or BIGINT and implies a primary key. INTEGER generation stops at 2147483647; BIGINT generation stops at 9223372036854775807.
At most one generated ROWVERSION column is permitted per table. Tokens come from a durable database-wide counter and the column cannot participate in keys, foreign keys, or indexes.
Single or composite INTEGER/TEXT primary keys are supported.
Single or composite INTEGER/TEXT unique keys are supported; tuples containing NULL do not conflict.

Child and ordered parent key types/collations must match. SET NULL requires every child column to be nullable and outside the primary key. SET DEFAULT requires a proven compatible literal default, or proven no/NULL default on a nullable non-key child column. Deferred matching remains unsupported.
Functions, subqueries, and parameters are not accepted in check expressions.

Column-only INTEGER/TEXT/REAL equality indexes are supported. REAL components use hashed equality and do not provide ordered or range scans. BLOB/rowversion, expression, partial, included-column, and sort-direction indexes are unsupported.
The body must parse, bind, scratch-apply, and catalog-compare.
Trigger bodies are bounded to INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements.
WHEN is represented by the parser and rejected with SyntaxError before catalog persistence.
Collection indexes are nonunique; range scans exclude array-element paths.
Every row assignment is coerced and validated against the column's logical SQL type descriptor before persistence.

evidence.assertion: The installed source defines the target object catalog and supported SQL DDL forms.
Check expressions are deterministic and row-local with bounded syntax.
Collections use document storage with bounded scalar, nested, and array-element index behavior.

Runtime tags include Null, Integer, Real, Text, Blob, and exact Decimal; persistent columns retain validated logical SQL type descriptors, including signed 32-bit INTEGER, BIGINT, BOOLEAN, temporal, and bit-string distinctions.

Foreign keys require compatible ordered parent keys and support immediate MATCH SIMPLE with RESTRICT, NO ACTION, CASCADE, eligible-child SET NULL, or proven-literal SET DEFAULT behavior for delete and update actions.
Quoted identifiers support embedded quotes, reject NUL, and are limited to 128 UTF-16 code units.

Indexes are column-only and constrained to INTEGER/TEXT/REAL key components with supported collations; REAL components use equality-only hashed keys while ordered and range access remains limited to supported INTEGER/TEXT shapes.
All write paths validate and normalize values against the persisted logical SQL type descriptor before storage.
INTEGER/TEXT primary and unique keys support single and composite forms with documented NULL tuple semantics.
A table may contain one generated ROWVERSION excluded from keys, foreign keys, and indexes; inserts and updates allocate durable database-wide tokens.
Views and bounded triggers exist, while trigger WHEN is rejected with SyntaxError before catalog persistence.
